rules.title: Cartwright Act Amendments – Prohibition on Common Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: California's antitrust law now bars businesses—including landlords and property managers—from using shared pricing algorithms to collude on rents or other prices, and from coercing others to follow an algorithm's pricing recommendations.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on common pricing algorithms used to collude or coerce pricing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any business using or distributing a 'common' pricing algorithm (one with two or more users that incorporates competitor data to influence prices or terms), including apartment rental companies; does not apply to single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm/proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.quoted_span: The Cartwright Act now expressly prohibits (1) using or distributing common algorithms to collude on pricing, and (2) coercing users to adopt algorithmic recommendations.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the business uses a 'common' algorithm (shared by multiple users and incorporating competitor data) versus a proprietary single-firm algorithm

rules.conflict_note: This is a general antitrust statute applicable to all industries, not a housing-specific rent-setting law; it is included here because the source explicitly identifies apartment rental companies as a targeted industry under recent algorithmic pricing enforcement actions.
